A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, models, and experiments. All main-text and appendix material is readable, including proofs, tables, figures, prompts, and code listings. The added background appendix and relocated content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original model evaluations on composition benchmarks and synthetic reasoning tasks, including numerical results in Tables 1–4, performance heatmaps, and multiplication error analyses.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains these original empirical results in Appendices B–E, including benchmark accuracies, prompting comparisons, error analyses, and PEN/PER Multi evaluations.

M1.justification: The SSM recurrence, input-dependent matrices, and CoT construction in Definitions 1–2 are unchanged. The revisions concern theoretical assumptions and constructed proof inputs, without introducing a different model, training objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Math-QA, BIG-Bench Hard, Temporal-NLI, SpaRTUN, multiplication, dynamic programming, Einstein’s puzzle, PEN, and PER Multi. Balanced parentheses and palindromes newly discussed in Section 6 are theoretical examples, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain GPT-4o, GPT-4, Jamba, Mamba, and S4-H3; the other corresponding experiments retain their original model subsets. The newly cited search and self-correction methods are discussed but not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: Sampling, accuracy metrics, model configurations, task-size ranges, and zero-shot/few-shot/CoT protocols are unchanged. This includes the default 500 test samples and the 250 Boolean expressions. Revised theoretical precision assumptions do not document changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The prompting comparisons, input-complexity sweeps, multiplication carry-error case study, shortcut/RIG analysis, and algorithmic-composition analyses are retained. Matching v2 Appendices A–D to v3 Appendices B–E reveals no added or removed analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Section 7 in both versions specifies three evaluations per task unless otherwise stated. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting, without additional seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the performance heatmaps retain identical numerical entries, and the qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports Math-QA accuracy of 51.8% for GPT-4o and 42.2% for Jamba in both versions. Relocated results do not constitute new findings.

T1.justification: Section 6 replaces Theorem 4’s O(L log N) simulation claim for polynomially bounded precision and dimension with a regular-language theorem for finite-precision, fixed-dimensional SSMs, adding Definition 3 and an FSM construction. Theorem 3 gains an explicit log-precision restriction. Section 4 also adds an initial argument token and updates its reduction accordingly.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory critical-insight paragraph, and conclusion replace the central multi-layer log-space claim with a finite-state/regular-language limitation. The conclusion also drops the claimed necessity of exponential scaling. However, introduction contribution 2 still asserts the earlier O(L log N) result.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially reframes the explanation of limitations around finite-state memory, nonregular languages, and hardware precision, adding balanced-parentheses and palindrome examples. Section 8 explicitly limits the analysis to models without search or self-correction augmentations and acknowledges that these mechanisms can mitigate limitations using additional resources.

D1.justification: Hardware, model versions, parameter counts, prompt examples, generation code, and generation hyperparameters are unchanged. The implementation material moves to relettered appendices, with no new code/data access information or reproducibility disclosure.

R1.justification: Section 8 adds a focused discussion of tree search/theorem proving and self-correction, citing Trinh, Polu and Sutskever, Lample, Wang, and Kumar and colleagues. It distinguishes these augmentations from the architectures studied. The two Merrill and Sabharwal 2023 bibliography entries represent the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The theoretical exposition is substantially revised through the rewritten and retitled Section 6, reframed conclusion, and new three-subsection background appendix. Existing appendices are relettered, and related-work paragraphs are added and removed. Most experimental prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 numbered figures and four tables retain their graphical content and design. Some displays are relocated or regrouped, notably Algorithm 1/Figure 3 and the multiplication prompts in Figures 6–7. Pages reflow and the header changes from preprint to ICLR 2025 publication status.

improvement.justification: v3 improves theoretical scope: Section 6 replaces v2’s proof that assumes logarithmic precision despite allowing polynomial precision with a narrower finite-state argument, and the conclusion removes the exponential-scaling claim. The added background and augmentation caveat improve interpretation. These gains remain incomplete because introduction contribution 2 still claims the removed O(L log N) result, while the new FSM proof contains inconsistent state-set and transition notation. The empirical evidence is unchanged.
